content:
Hi, this is my first post here, so apologies if I've not chosen the right place for this post! I believe I've managed to (vibe-)formalise the result in the title of this topic: as the subject of my PhD, it was a fairly natural and interesting choice for me. I've been targeting the Lax Archive, as it seems to take an approach which broadly makes sense to me. Here it is on gitlab pages.

I didn't rely on any existing Lax submissions, so I hope i didn't miss any opportunities to reuse existing work. As it stands, the most relevant contributions to that archive might be elements of the background work, most notable perhaps other ergodic theorems (I understand that Birkhoff may make its way into Mathlib at some point, but this work also needed a few variations of Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem).

I'd like to get to the point of running lax register to submit the work for review. I wonder if anyone might have any particular advice before doing so - the original paper is very much human-written, but while I've tried to make sure the natural language wordings of statements are clear and not too idiosyncratic, I've heavily relied on Claude in producing this work. I imagine it may make sense to split the work up into multiple submissions - but I'm not sure if the way Lax allows you to pick and choose existing results to use as dependencies of your new work might mean it's not necessary.
This topic was moved here from #maths > The multiplicative ergodic theorem by Chris Henson.
